source_head_policy: Latest commit returned by GitHub commit search during this review. A commit pin proves provenance only, not safety.

repositories.use: TypeScript/JavaScript technical-indicator implementations for independent formula comparison only.
risks: Latest repository commit surfaced is 2020-03-16; npm 3.1.0 was published years ago.
Legacy TypeScript 2.x and older build/test dependencies require compatibility and supply-chain review.
Indicator names such as VWAP/OBV/volume profile do not establish valid traded volume for Deriv synthetic indices.

repositories.use: Backtrader-based research/backtesting framework with strategies, market-data fetchers, CLI and MCP server; evaluate architecture and test methodology only.
risks: GPL-3.0 compatibility must be resolved before any code reuse or distribution.
Broad dependencies include data-provider, numerical, plotting and MCP packages.
No evidence yet of Deriv synthetic-index data fidelity, contract/cost modelling, no-lookahead validation or reproducible out-of-sample results.

repositories.use: React 19+/StyleX design system; potentially useful only as a separate UI design reference.
risks: Not a trading, risk, execution or research capability.
Repository is very large; no reason to clone or import it into the trading runtime.

repositories.use: Native Rust CLI for AI-driven browser automation and accessibility-tree interaction.
risks: Node.js 22+ and native binary/browser installation are required.
Browser control can reach authenticated sessions if misconfigured; use disposable profiles and synthetic logins only.
Review launcher, postinstall, browser permissions, downloads, network egress and credential storage before execution.

repositories.license_observed: MIT (LICENSE.md; SKILL.md frontmatter also declares MIT)
repositories.use: Read-only codebase audit and self-contained implementation-plan skill; optional dispatch to a separate executor worktree. Potential project-local Claude skill after isolation and permission review.
risks: The inspected skill is explicitly read-only on source code and may create or modify plan files only under plans/ or advisor-plans/.

Its execute variant dispatches a separate executor subagent in an isolated git worktree; the skill says it does not merge, push or commit. Verify the host's actual worktree isolation before enabling dispatch.
The optional --issues mode publishes GitHub issues and therefore requires explicit user approval; do not enable it by default.
The repository has a small 16-blob tree; inspected README, LICENSE.md, SKILL.md, audit playbook and plan template. No full runtime/security testing was needed because no executable is installed.

repositories.use: Engineering lifecycle skills for spec, plan, build, test, review, web performance, simplify and ship workflows.
risks: Commands such as /build auto and /ship can trigger multi-step implementation or release work.
Review each skill's tools, hooks, file/network access and approval boundaries before enabling it.
Do not allow skill instructions to override AURELIA release authority or independent review.

repositories.use: Codex Security CLI, TypeScript SDK and GitHub Action for source scanning, finding validation, patch proposals and reports.
risks: CLI/CI usage requires an API key or Codex Security credential; do not expose production secrets to scanner jobs.
Review source upload, cloud processing, retention, telemetry, report publishing and permissions before scanning proprietary AURELIA code.
Security findings require human/independent validation; scanner output cannot approve its own patches or releases.

repositories.use: Educational Java algorithm and data-structure implementations; consult for concepts only.
risks: Not a trading strategy library or validated quantitative implementation.
Do not port algorithms into production without independent mathematical specification, tests and performance review.
Repository targets Java 21 and includes test/build dependencies; no runtime need established.

repositories.use: GitHub JavaScript Action that obtains penv-cloud secrets through GitHub OIDC and supplies them only to a specified command process.
repositories.recommended_ref_policy: Pin full 40-character commit SHA only after complete source review; upstream README explicitly rejects mutable tags.
risks: Action executes a command with external secrets in its process environment.
Upstream action.yml/README explicitly state it does not protect against a malicious step in the same job; revocation is best-effort and short server TTL is a separate control.
Only README, action.yml, package.json, main.mjs and post.mjs were inspected; api/delivery/revocation implementation and complete tests remain unaudited.
Do not add duplicate action steps; do not add to AURELIA production CI or deliver Deriv/broker/production credentials.

limitations: The audit is a targeted source review of selected high-risk entrypoints and complete source tree for shadcn/improve, not a complete line-by-line audit of all repositories.
No upstream code or action was executed; no SBOM, dependency vulnerability scan, secret scan, malware scan or dynamic sandbox test was produced.
No external runtime (ClaudeCode, JEV, Dev, DeepSeek Harness, Hermes or PlaywrightCLI) was proven connected or executed during this audit.
The Penv action's same-job threat boundary is not suitable for secrets in workflows that also run untrusted steps; its principal source files and unit tests were inspected but not executed.
Codex Security was not run against AURELIA source because provider credentials, source processing and retention approvals were not established.
TheAlgorithms/Java and the large Astryx repository were not line-by-line audited because their initial fit is reference-only or unrelated.

findings.finding: Same-job secret exposure is explicitly out of scope. It uses GitHub OIDC, obtains a penv credential, and runs the caller command with secret values in that child process environment. Revocation is best-effort; security depends on server-side short TTL. The action itself explicitly warns a malicious same-job step can read runner process memory and steal secrets.
findings.decision: Do not use in AURELIA CI or any job containing untrusted steps; never deliver Deriv/broker/production secrets.

findings.finding: Postinstall may download a native binary from a GitHub release URL and follows redirects; no checksum/signature verification was observed in the inspected postinstall path. Browser tooling exposes powerful page interaction, JavaScript evaluation, upload and network inspection capabilities.
findings.decision: Sandbox-only; require immutable package/binary provenance verification, isolated browser profile, synthetic data and restricted egress.

findings.finding: GitHub Action passes selected provider credentials to the scanner runtime, supports deep repository scans, and can upload validated findings artifacts. Its runtime constructs a restricted environment and uses Codex sandbox preflight; on eligible GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners it may use sudo to install bubblewrap/AppArmor when sandbox setup is unavailable.
findings.decision: Do not scan proprietary AURELIA source until source-processing, data retention, provider, permission, artifact and cost policies are approved. Test only a synthetic repository first.

findings.finding: MCP exposes backtest and data-fetch tools accepting caller-supplied local configuration/data/output paths and performs filesystem reads/writes and network data fetches. It is not a multi-tenant isolated execution boundary; the codebase is GPL-3.0 and the inspected workflow targets stocks/crypto/forex/VIX rather than Deriv synthetic indices.
findings.decision: Research-only; do not expose its MCP server to untrusted clients or AURELIA runtime. No import before GPL compatibility, path-confinement, dependency, data/cost and no-lookahead audits.

findings.finding: MIT-licensed read-only advisor skill; writes plans only. Optional execute dispatches a separate executor worktree and --issues can create GitHub issues.
findings.decision: Selective skill candidate only after confirming actual host worktree isolation and keeping issue creation disabled without explicit approval.

findings.finding: MIT collection includes optional hooks and workflow skills. Session-start hook injects skill text only when wired; shipping skill is operational guidance and should not itself be treated as release approval.
findings.decision: Selective reference use; no hooks or bulk skill install. AURELIA release authority remains separate.

findings.finding: Old TypeScript indicator library; package/toolchain age and indicator semantics require parity checks.
findings.decision: Formula reference only; no dependency adoption.

findings.finding: Large React/StyleX design-system repository with no AURELIA trading-system fit.
findings.decision: No trading-runtime adoption; no full source audit justified.

findings.finding: Educational algorithm implementations; no direct AURELIA trading capability established.
